issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may reappraise evidence in a special leave appeal when the High Court has missed the decisive issue, discredited evidence on erroneous grounds, and thereby risked grave injustice.
material_facts: The complainant brought a special leave appeal after the High Court altered the respondents’ murder convictions and reduced their sentences; the State did not appeal.
The High Court gave no cogent analysis of the evidence and relied on a statement made during investigation by a person who was not examined at trial.
The Supreme Court considered the record because it concluded that the High Court had missed the real point and had reached its conclusion on erroneous grounds.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court was justified in examining the evidence to determine whether grave injustice had resulted.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court does not ordinarily reappraise evidence to decide whether the High Court reached the correct factual conclusion. It may do so where the High Court has missed the real point requiring determination, discredited evidence on erroneous grounds, and failed to consider circumstances indicating a risk of grave injustice. The High Court’s powers in an appeal from conviction under section 386 of the Code of Criminal Procedure include reappraising the evidence and reaching its own conclusion on the record.

rule.if: special_leave_criminal_appeal and high_court_missed_decisive_issue and high_court_discredited_evidence_on_erroneous_grounds and record_indicated_risk_of_grave_injustice

predicates.special_leave_criminal_appeal: A complainant brought a special leave appeal in a criminal case after the High Court altered the accused persons’ convictions or sentences.
predicates.high_court_missed_decisive_issue: The High Court did not address the decisive issue raised by the evidence in the case.
predicates.high_court_discredited_evidence_on_erron: The High Court rejected or discounted evidence on grounds that were not supported by a proper assessment of the record.
predicates.record_indicated_risk_of_grave_injustice: The record contained circumstances suggesting that the High Court’s approach could have resulted in grave injustice.

issues.definition: When a complainant brings a special leave appeal in a criminal case and the High Court misses the decisive issue, discredits evidence on erroneous grounds, and the record indicates a risk of grave injustice, the Supreme Court may reappraise the evidence.

issues.legal_issue: Intentionally inflicting fatal injuries while exceeding a right of private defence supports a conviction for culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Part I.
material_facts: The prosecution evidence came from interested witnesses, and most of the accused had also sustained injuries that the witnesses did not truthfully explain.
The evidence indicated that a melee arose from an altercation and that the respondents probably used force while exercising a right of private defence.
The circumstances did not justify causing death, and the respondents exceeded that right.
The injuries were intentionally inflicted and were sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
issues.conclusion: The respondents’ convictions under section 304 Part I of the Indian Penal Code were maintained.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 304 Part I of the Indian Penal Code, culpable homicide not amounting to murder is punishable where the act is done with the requisite intention. A person who uses force in private defence but exceeds that right may be liable for the resulting culpable homicide. The Court maintained the conviction under section 304 Part I rather than the original conviction under section 302.

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case was a criminal appeal concerning the accused persons’ convictions.
predicates.probable_private_defence: The evidence indicated that the accused probably used force while defending themselves or others.
predicates.circumstances_did_not_justify_causing_de: The circumstances of the encounter did not justify causing the victim’s death.
predicates.intentional_injuries_sufficient_to_cause: The accused intentionally inflicted injuries sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns probable private defence, the circumstances did not justify causing death, and the accused intentionally inflicted injuries sufficient to cause death, the culpable-homicide conviction under Part I is maintained.

issues.legal_issue: A custodial sentence should be enhanced when the sentence imposed is grossly inadequate in light of the gravity and circumstances of the offence.
material_facts: The respondents had served less than six months in custody, and the High Court reduced their imprisonment to the period already undergone.
The offence was grave, and the High Court gave no particular reason for imposing such a short custodial sentence.
The Supreme Court concluded that the sentence was grossly and entirely inadequate and enhanced it to five years’ rigorous imprisonment.
issues.conclusion: The custodial sentence was enhanced to five years’ rigorous imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: In fixing punishment, a court should consider the nature of the offence, the circumstances in which it was committed, and the degree of deliberation shown by the offender. The punishment should be proportionate to the gravity of the offence; a sentence that is grossly and entirely inadequate may involve a failure of justice.

rule.if: criminal_appeal and grave_offence and sentence_limited_to_short_time_served and no_reason_given_for_short_sentence

predicates.criminal_appeal: The case was a criminal appeal concerning the sentence imposed on the accused.
predicates.grave_offence: The offence for which the accused were sentenced was grave.
predicates.sentence_limited_to_short_time_served: The custodial sentence was limited to a short period that the accused had already served.
predicates.no_reason_given_for_short_sentence: The court imposing the short sentence gave no particular reason for doing so.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a grave offence and the custodial sentence is limited to a short time already served without a stated reason, the custodial sentence is enhanced.
